result:
Audit complete. I read the full notebook (59 cells, including a 4-section correction history) and `context.md`, then wrote `AUDIT_REPORT.md` in the project root.

**Result: all 15 subcriteria PASA** — for the project's declared final model (Random Forest, `n_estimators=300`, trained on the deduplication-corrected data from section 10).

The most notable finding, documented in detail in the report: the **original** Random Forest failed V4.2 — diesel (`Fuel Type=D`) RMSE was 1.24× the global RMSE (threshold ≤1.10), because 98 test rows had a "twin" in training due to `Make`/`Model` capitalization duplicates (`drop_duplicates()` missed case-only differences, e.g. "Colorado ZR2 4WD" vs "COLORADO ZR2 4WD"). The notebook tried two other fixes first (sample weighting, then a CV-selected alternative) — both failed to close the gap — before tracing it to the actual duplicate-detection bug and fixing it at the source (normalize case before deduplicating, before the split). That corrected model is what the project declares final, and on it all four evaluable fuel-type subgroups pass the ≤1.10 threshold (diesel lands at 1.0040).

No actions recommended — no FALLA or NO SE PUEDE DETERMINAR results. The report also flags one judgment call transparently: the project itself notes the root cause was found "looking at the test set," which I did not treat as a V3.1 violation since it's a uniform data-cleaning fix rather than a hyperparameter/threshold chosen to game test performance — but I documented it so you can judge that nuance yourself.
